newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest-July 16.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest-July 16.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

FRANKFURT - The co-owner of German advertising agency Tostmann & Wulfes, Tom Tostmann, confirms his partner, Thomas Wulfes, is considering leaving the agency and that they are discussing a possible sell-off. "We are talking about the future," Tostmann says, adding he expects a final decision about Wulfes' future with the agency to be reached in the next two days. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Publicis Communications tops the ranks of European advertising networks for 1996 in Campaign magazine. Publicis represented billings volume of $4.616 billion. Euro RSCG fell from the number one spot to the fourth. Second place goes to Young & Rubicam and third is held by Ogilvy & Mather Europe.
(Horizont)

FRANKFURT - Frankfurt ad agency DSB&K ends its cooperation with jewelry and watch retailer Christ due to differences in their advertising concepts. The account is worth about 15 million marks ($8.4 million). Christ was the largest full-service client of the Frankfurt agency. (Horizont)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

FRANKFURT - Commercial bank Commerzbank AG and the country's largest retailer Karstadt AG say they will allow consumers to shop on the Internet with credit cards. The two companies will allow Commerzbank customers with Eurocard credit cards as well as users of Karstadt and Hertie customer cards to buy goods from Karstadt's "My-World" shopping mall on the World Wide Web.
(http://www.my-world.de) (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - After years when Germans avoided movie theatres in droves, the cinema is enjoying a heyday not seen in almost two decades, a new study shows. More than seven percent of Germans over 14 years old see a movie at least once a week, according to the Allensbacher Market and Advertising Media Analysis (AWA 97) by the Institute of Opinion Polling. (Reuter)

BERLIN - German films come up aces again. Six months into the year only three movies - all German - manage to cross the magic 3-million-admissions benchmark here to achieve a Golden Screen Award. While the first quarter's remarkable 37 percent market share for domestic pics has leveled out to a still-respectable 24.4 percent, German pics have notched up grosses of 156.6 million marks. (Variety)

BERLIN - U.S. media company Metromedia International Inc has takes over Berlin talk radio station NewsTalk 93.6, the German station says. Metromedia bought 70 percent of the station's shares while 30 percent remains with media investor Frank Otto and media company Europa Plus GmbH. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - German newspapers saw a slight fall in their number of readers because of increasing competition from magazines over the last year, an advertising industry study says. According to the Allensbach Market and Advertising Media Analysis by the Institute of Opinion Polling, newspaper readership sank two percent due to more magazines appearing on the market. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

LEVERKUSEN - Bayer AG says it will invest $68 million to raise annual capacity by 75,000 tonnes at a U.S. plant where it manufactures synthetic rubber. Bayer said the expansion project at its plant in Orange, Texas, will raise output of polybutadiene and solution styrenebutadiene rubber, which are used in tyre and plastic manufacturing. (Reuter)

MUNICH - Intel Corp just beat expectations for second-quarter results, but Europe stands out as a weak spot for the world's largest chip maker. Second-quarter sales in Europe rose only three percent to $1.43 billion -- well off the company's worldwide sales growth rate of 29 percent. (Reuter)

BONN - Defence and electronics group Rheinmetall AG says it will take management control of Badenwerk Holding AG's electronics business via a share swap between the two partners' subsidiaries. Under the deal, utility Badenwerk will sell 75.5 percent of Kommunikations Industrie Holding and all of Kreutler GmbH to Rheinmetall Elektronik AG, a unit of Rheinmetall.
(Reuter)

INGOLSTADT - Audi AG, the luxury car unit of Volkswagen AG, says sales of its top-model A8 sedan surged in the first half of 1997 as production rose 49 percent to 7,177 vehicles. Audi says sales in Germany rose 13 percent to about 3,800 vehicles during the period from January to June and that its market share of the domestic luxury segment rose to about 22 percent from 17.5 percent in the year-ago period. (Reuter)

COLOGNE - Ford-Werke says its German market share remained at 11.3 percent during the first half of the year but its market share improved to 12.8 percent in June from 11.0 percent in the year-ago period. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - German carmaker shares, particularly Volkswagen AG, are getting fresh fuel to keep up their unprecedented advance as analysts say the sector will stay among the best European performers. (Reuter)

LUDWIGSHAFEN - BASF AG says it will form a joint venture with Algerian oil and gas company Sonatrach to build a propane dehydrogenation plant that will produce propylene at a BASF affiliate site in Spain. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:
WALLDORF - Matthias Born, distribution director and director of sales marketing at publishing house Spiegel-Verlag, becomes director of marketing at the Sueddeutscher Verlag. (Kress)
WALLDORF - Barbara Kothe, previously marketing director of publishing group Weltbild, will become marketing director for specialty books at the Carl Hanser Verlag in Munich on September 1. (Kress)
